This dispatch office runs a trucking company from your map's own loading and unloading stations.

GET STARTED
1. Buy the Transport Company HQ from the shop under Buildings > Sheds and place it on your farm.
2. The contract board fills the moment it is standing.
3. Buy a truck: only vehicles the game classes as trucks enrol in the Fleet tab.
4. Pick a job on the Dispatch tab, accept it, and haul the load yourself or hire a driver.

A guide to each section is on the next pages.

Jobs come from stations that hold goods, priced against the live economy and the route length.

BULK FREIGHT moves liters of grain, roots or silage.
PALLET FREIGHT moves palletisable goods and is counted in pallets (1000 L each).

Every job has a pickup, a drop-off, an amount, a reward and a deadline.

TIERS
Standard: the usual job.
Urgent: half the deadline, more pay.
Bulk: more volume, tighter margin.

The amount is sized to your fleet, so a job never asks for more than a few loads of your biggest truck and trailer. The detail panel shows the distance, estimated fuel cost and estimated profit before you accept.

Only jobs you can actually LOAD are offered. The game only shows a loading prompt at stations your farm owns or can access (your own silos and buildings, public buying points), so sources are limited to those. If a station you own is empty, fill it or let a production build up stock first.

HAUL IT YOURSELF
Load at the pickup, tip at the destination. Progress climbs as you tip, and the reward lands when it completes. The truck that physically tips is credited, so your own driving shows in the Fleet tab.

HIRE A DRIVER
Hands the route to the base game AI. The driver keeps a share of the reward as their wage. When the job is done the truck drives itself back to the HQ.

A job you accepted for yourself can still be handed to a driver later.

Over-delivering is never wasted: surplus rolls onto your next open job for the same goods.

THE DRIVERS TAB
Hire named drivers, assign each to a truck, and fire them when you want. Drivers earn a weekly wage from your balance and gain experience with every completed contract, which raises their wage. Your driver cap grows with reputation and HQ tier.

REPUTATION
Delivering on time builds reputation; missing a deadline costs it. Higher reputation means more drivers on the payroll.

HQ UPGRADES
Spend money to raise the HQ tier for a bigger board and more driver capacity.

MAINTENANCE
Trucks need a service every 5000 km. The Fleet tab tells you when one is due; the bill is booked on the truck.

The Ledger tab keeps company totals: revenue, driver wages, fuel, distance and job count, plus a history of every finished and expired contract, newest first.

It also shows a rolling weekly profit and loss, so you can see the company trending rather than just the lifetime totals.

Company figures are kept separate from the per-truck books on purpose. A load you haul yourself is credited to the truck that tipped, but the company ledger keeps one consistent total no matter how a job was run.

A hired driver usually recovers on its own, but on busy roads or tight farmyards it can get wedged. The mod watches for this and replans the route up to three times, then recalls the driver.

IF THE TRUCK STOPS MOVING
1. Press H to take control of the truck and stop the AI job.
2. Drive the truck a short way out of the jam, or turn it around to face open road.
3. Open the Dispatch tab and find the contract.
4. Press Hire driver again. The AI replans from the truck's current position and continues the route.

You can hand any accepted job to a driver, even one you took yourself, so nothing is lost when a route goes wrong.

The Settings tab covers the whole company.

Company enabled: master switch.
Contracts on the board: 1-12, default 5.
Deadline (days): 1-30, default 7.
Driver wage share: 0-100%, default 20%.
Return truck to HQ: on by default; off leaves a finished truck where it ended.
Notifications: on/off.
Debug logging: per player, off by default.

In multiplayer, each farm that owns an HQ runs its own company with its own board, fleet, ledger and settings. Only the server can change shared settings; debug logging is always editable.
